description: Musk F-35 / drone-swarm statement with Forbes corroboration and primary X post text.
pasted_text:
PRIMARY (X, 24–25 Nov 2024 timeframe; Forbes reports 26 Nov 2024):
Musk references a viral video of large-scale coordinated drone swarms and posts on X that some are still building manned fighter jets like the F-35. In follow-up replies he argues the F-35 design was broken at the requirements level (too many roles for too many customers), calling it expensive and complex; argues manned fighter jets are obsolete in the age of drones; says crewed fighters are an inefficient way to extend missile range or drop bombs compared with reusable drones; cites sophisticated SAM/drone threats as shown in the Russia–Ukraine conflict; and calls for stopping the F-35 program as poor military value for money while saying some other US weapons systems are good though overpriced.

Forbes (David Hambling) covers the posts: https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidhambling/2024/11/26/elon-musk-calls-f-35-builders-idiots-favors-drone-swarms/
X status: https://twitter.com/elonmusk/status/1860574377013838033
facts: On or about 24–25 Nov 2024, Musk posts on X after referencing a viral video of large-scale coordinated drone swarms.
Musk criticises continued construction of manned fighter jets such as the F-35 in favour of drone-swarm approaches.
In follow-up X replies, Musk says the F-35 design was broken at the requirements level because it was required to be too many things to too many people, making it expensive and complex.

Musk argues manned fighter jets are obsolete in the age of drones and that crewed fighters will get pilots killed against sophisticated SAM or drone threats, citing the Russia–Ukraine conflict as an example.
Musk says crewed fighter jets are an inefficient way to extend missile range or drop bombs compared with reusable drones that avoid pilot overhead.
Musk writes that some US weapons systems are good but overpriced and urges ending the F-35 program as the worst military value for money in history among US systems he references.
Forbes publishes coverage of the posts on 26 Nov 2024.

subject_quotes.text: It's a shit design…The F-35 design was broken at the requirements level, because it was required to be too many things to too many people. This made it an expensive & complex jack of all trades, master of none.
